# spacetrace

> Disk usage tool that answers "what grew?". It scans a disk, writes the result
> to a SQLite snapshot, and compares two snapshots to name the folder that
> filled up — rather than only showing what is large right now. There is a
> desktop app with an interactive treemap, a command line tool, a server agent
> that scans unattended, and a hub that watches a fleet of machines.

Deliberately not version-specific: the current version, file names and release
notes live on the pages linked below, which are generated from the release
itself. No version number is written into this file, because nothing would
keep it true.

## What it measures, and why the numbers differ from other tools

- Two sizes, never mixed: `size` is file bytes only, `alloc` is what the disk
  actually holds, including directory blocks.
- `alloc` tracks `df`, not `du`. With no shared blocks the two agree. With
  sharing, `du` over-counts by exactly the shared blocks: it deduplicates
  hardlinks but not APFS clones, which have their own inode while the data sits
  on disk once. spacetrace deduplicates both.
- Capacity is reported as free of total, never as a "% used" figure. On a
  filesystem whose space is shared between volumes — an APFS container, btrfs
  subvolumes, thin LVM — a used figure would include the siblings and disagree
  with `df` about the same mount.
- Sparse files are the reason the measure is a parameter and not a default: a
  file can report up to 50 times what it holds, and those are the biggest
  entries on a real disk.
- Symbolic links are not followed and count with their own size. Hardlinked
  files are counted once.
- btrfs and ZFS real usage is reported wrongly today, because of reflinks and
  compression. This is a known gap, not a claim.

## Components and licensing

- The scanner, snapshot store, diff, the `spacetrace` command line tool and the
  `spacetrace-agent` server agent are Apache-2.0 and public.
- The desktop app and the hub are proprietary and are not buildable from
  source. That is the trade for the core staying permissively licensed.
- The agent deletes nothing outside its own snapshot database. That is a
  decision, so software installed on somebody's server can earn trust, not a
  missing feature.

## Pages

- [Home](https://spacetrace.teknobakkall.com/): what the tool does, with an
  interactive treemap that also renders without JavaScript.
- [Desktop app](https://spacetrace.teknobakkall.com/desktop/): the treemap
  window, for macOS, Windows and Linux.
- [Command line and agent](https://spacetrace.teknobakkall.com/cli/): scan,
  snapshot, diff, and reading a remote machine over HTTP. One static binary,
  Apache-2.0.
- [Hub](https://spacetrace.teknobakkall.com/hub/): fleet dashboard, growth
  trend, threshold alerts. Self-hosted, Linux and macOS.
- [Download](https://spacetrace.teknobakkall.com/download/): every file for
  every platform, with the current version and checksums.
- [Guide](https://spacetrace.teknobakkall.com/guide/): installing, the
  commands, the flags, and what each reported number means.
- [Changelog](https://spacetrace.teknobakkall.com/changelog/): what changed in
  each released version of all three components.

## Install

The command line tool and the agent, on macOS and Linux:

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/unalcakir28/spacetrace/main/install.sh | sh
```

The desktop app and the hub have their own installers, listed on the download
page. Every downloadable file for all three components is published in the
public core repository, so none of them needs a credential to fetch.

## Source

- [Core repository](https://github.com/unalcakir28/spacetrace): the nine crates
  behind the command line tool and the agent, Apache-2.0. Architecture and
  design decisions are documented in its `docs/` directory.

## Other languages

Every page above exists in five languages. English carries no prefix; the
others are `/tr/`, `/it/`, `/fr/` and `/de/` — for example
`https://spacetrace.teknobakkall.com/de/download/`. The English page is the
`x-default`.
